items.title: Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan at Money2020 Cybercrime Becoming ‘Extremely Quick’
items.summary:
Why is it so difficult to recover stolen cryptocurrency, and how are cybersecurity firms working to stop attacks before they happen?

At Money20/20 USA in Las Vegas, JD Durkin speaks with Ido Ben-Natan, Co-Founder and CEO of Blockaid, about the growing threat of crypto-related cyberattacks, the challenges of recovering stolen digital assets, and the technologies being developed to prevent breaches before funds disappear.

Ben-Natan explains how Blockaid works with major digital asset platforms and financial institutions, including Coinbase (NASDAQ: COIN), Kraken, Gemini, Fidelity, and BNY (NYSE: BK), to help identify threats, prevent fraud, and secure blockchain transactions.

The conversation centers on findings from Blockaid's latest cybersecurity research, which highlights more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency stolen through major hacks during the year and the significant challenges victims face when attempting to recover lost funds.

Ben-Natan discusses why digital assets can be particularly vulnerable to theft, noting that transactions can be executed and funds moved across wallets within seconds, often leaving security teams with little time to react. He also explains how blockchain transparency allows investigators to track stolen assets while still making recovery difficult when funds move across jurisdictions or remain under the control of malicious actors.

Additional topics include emerging cybersecurity threats, the increasing pace of crypto-related attacks, incident response challenges, and how security teams are adapting to an environment where threats can develop in minutes rather than days.

The interview also explores Blockaid's preventative security approach, including transaction simulation technology designed to identify suspicious activity and potential risks before transactions are executed on-chain.

Looking ahead, Ben-Natan expects organizations across the digital asset ecosystem to place greater emphasis on proactive security measures, automated threat detection, transaction monitoring, and real-time response capabilities as cyber threats continue to evolve.
